elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall pay Vendor no liquidated damages"
"and no penalty" (replacing "fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week")

elements.element: Any early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: Condition absent: 9.4 "Customer owes only accrued Fees, and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees" — no early-termination fee exists

elements.element: Such fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall pay Vendor no liquidated damages and no penalty" — no other liquidated amount remains

reasons: The single replacement negates the 15%-of-annual-Fees weekly liquidated damages charge in Section 7.7, delivering the preferred position that no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by Customer.
Fallback is also satisfied on its face: no early-termination fee is imposed anywhere (9.4 limits Customer to accrued Fees), so the cap condition is demonstrably absent.

Edit is confined to the offending sentence; Section 7.3 dispute/interest protection and Section 9.4 termination economics are untouched, and Vendor's other late-payment remedies elsewhere are unaffected.
The retained trigger wording ("If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date") is slightly redundant but introduces no undefined term, contradiction, or dangling obligation.
